correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the exact Orlicz point-evaluation norm and proves the discrete simultaneous-law criterion using weighted empirical SLLN, second Borel–Cantelli and uniform boundedness. Exact finite abelian group automorphism counts yield the squared-column entropy. A convergent square-partition Euler product gives the upper 1/3 growth exponent; 2^{m-1} disjoint constrained groups give the lower exponent. The inverse Young-function estimate and strict inclusion in larger-than-moment Orlicz spaces are proved. A packaged Python checker independently verifies the small-order structural identities. Excludes beta=1/3 and any extrapolation to actual class groups.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 work explicitly distinguishes useful test classes for Cohen–Lenstra class-group heuristics. The result identifies an arithmetic, sharp away from equality, one-third phase boundary in a natural near-L1 Orlicz scale, proves a simultaneous strong law on a class strictly larger than the positive-moment union, and constructs almost-sure counterexamples below the boundary. Both sides are explained by the nontrivial partitions-into-squares entropy mechanism. It is not a finite table, a mere renaming, or a routine specialized L^q consequence.
